newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's navy to hold 10-day exercises in Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Iran's navy to hold 10-day exercises in Gulf.

text.p: Iran's navy will conduct a 10-day military manoeuvre involving 10,000 troops in the Gulf region next week, Iran's navy commander said on Saturday.

Rear Admiral Ali Shamkhani told reporters the exercise, which is due to begin on November 21, was a "show of navy force, defence readiness and a means of elevating coordination between various participating (Iranian armed) forces".
He said about 100 vessels, including submarines, would participate in the manoeuvre in Iranian and international waters, supported by 40 airplanes and helicopters.
Shamkhani said Iran's third Kilo-class Russian submarine would leave Russia for Iran on the first day of the exercises. He did not say when it was expected to arrive.

Iran -- which has repeatedly said its rearmament was only for self-defence purposes -- is the only Gulf state to deploy submarines in the region which has about 70 percent of the world's oil reserves.
Speaking at navy headquarters in Tehran, Shamkhani said the manoeuvre "does not challenge anyone and does not signal any tension."

Shamkhani reiterated Iran's opposition to the presence of Western naval forces in the Gulf. "The presence of 90, mostly American, naval ships in the Persian Gulf is a kind of occupation which only creates tension in the region," he said.
